changes: Updated Lattice-Parallel-Development-Capability.md with an authority/evidence mode matrix using the existing off, shadow, enforce, and receipt-backed-l2-plus vocabulary; added a detailed Baseline 2-5 Parallel Implementation Plan with Layer 1 status, 2 CLI hosts, 8 workstream/review agents, 1 coordinator, ownership, sequential proof, integration, stop, rollback, and DONE criteria.
usage: Open Lattice-Parallel-Development-Capability.md and read Authority Modes And Evidence Chains plus Baseline 2-5 Parallel Implementation Plan before starting parallel baseline implementation. Use it to assign Codex/Claude hosts, freeze shared schema, keep Production Safety shadow-only, keep Claim fail-closed, and prove layers sequentially.
expectedOutcome: User can see exactly whether Layer 1 is ready and how many hosts and agents to use for parallel implementation without confusing implementation speed with capability proof or receipt-backed authority.
actualTranscript: lattice validate --story=B-cd0b --json --forceTakeover passed; npm test ran npm run test:e2e and node packages/main/dist/tasks/cli-e2e.js, ending with ALL PASS; verification coverage was 6/6; reviewer findings F-001 and F-002 were resolved.
outcomeDiff: No user-visible gap remains. Layer 1 runner support exists, but formal Layer 1 proof remains incomplete until independent review evidence and a PASS baseline-suite-report.json exist, so higher-layer claims stay locked.
limitations: This story updates the execution document only. It does not implement a runtime scheduler, receipt verification, authority enforcement, or a new capability claim.
pitfalls: The initial document used drifted terms local/off, receipt-backed-authority, and authorityReceiptRefs; reviewer findings forced alignment to off|shadow|enforce, receipt-backed-l2-plus, and authority.receiptRefs. Worktree validate required npm run build because dist was missing.
